newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-ELS, WESTNER KEEP SOUTH AFRICA ON TOP. [CORRECTED 18:53 GMT]
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS, WESTNER KEEP SOUTH AFRICA ON TOP. [CORRECTED 18:53 GMT]

text.p: Last-hole birdies by Ernie Els and Wayne Westner hoisted South Africa back into the lead of the World Cup of Golf after the second round at Erinvale on Friday.
The South Africans had gone into the day leading by one shot but had dropped behind Scotland by the time they played the 18th.
But Westner struck his second shot to 20 feet and holed for his birdie while Els hit his 130-yard approach to eight feet and made it as well.
Both carded level-par 72s to reach eight under par with Scotland a stroke behind after rounds of 70 from Paul Lawrie and 72 by Andrew Coltart.

Denmark and France (corrects from China) were joint third on 285 while the U.S. defending champions made a concerted charge on a day of generally high scoring with Steve Jones and Tom Lehman each carding two-under-par 70s.
That leaves them fifth on 286, six shots behind the South Africans as they attempt to capture the title which Fred Couples and Davis Love won for the last four years.
Els, the world number four, had four birdies and four bogeys in his 72 but was discontent afterwards.
"I really didn't play well," he said. "I putted very poorly and didn't hit the ball well. Wayne played better than me but ended up with the same score. We kind of just hung in there."
Lawrie, a late replacement in the event for Sam Torrance, moved level with German Bernhard Langer in the chase for individual honours. Both are five under after two rounds.
Lawrie's partner Coltart said they were looking forward to going head-to-head with South Africa on Saturday.
"They are probably finding it harder than us as there must be an incredible amount of pressure on them," said Coltart.
"They were favourites from the moment their team was announced but no one gave us a chance."

Meanwhile, Chile were disqualified after Guillermo Encina signed for an incorrect score. Encina signed his marker's card for a finish of five and four at the last two holes when he had actually made four and five.
